Corrections to Mana et al. (2026)

This article documents two errors found after publication of Mana et al. (2026) and lists every published result affected by their correction. Both errors were reported by elliottower in issues #20 and #21. The corrections were made by Jožka Mana and have not been reviewed by the other authors or by the journal. None of the conclusions of the article change.

What was wrong

  1. MoCA threshold. Table 1 of the article states that MoCA-based algorithms define global cognitive deficit as MoCA < 27. The code applied MoCA < 26, the same value as was stated in the Appendix to the article. The code now applies MoCA < 27, as stated in the article.

  2. Missing data in the concordance analysis. The Methods state that analyses were done on complete cases (N = 190). The concordance statistics (Cohen’s κ, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) were instead computed on all cases available for each pair of algorithms (N = 190 to 202). They are now computed on the 190 complete cases, as stated in the article.

The values printed in the article are distributed with the package as rates_published and concords_published. Version 1.2.0 of the package reproduces the article as printed:

devtools::install_github("josefmana/demcrit@v1.2.0")

Changed statements

In addition, the following tables and figures change accordingly: Table A3 (rates per algorithm), Tables A4 and A5 (best and worst approximations of Level II), Figure 1 (dot sizes and bold edges), Figure 2 and Figures A7 to A9 (concordance matrices), and Figures A4 to A6 (rates and their demographic predictors).

What does not change

  • The range and median of PDD rate estimates (2.11% to 16.84%, Md = 4.21%), and all algorithms using FAQ item 9 to define IADL deficit.
  • Cohen’s κ among algorithms using FAQ item 9 (0.86, SD = 0.09).
  • All MMSE-based, sMoCA-based and Level II algorithms.
  • The exploratory variable selection, the screening model (MoCA Five words and MMSE Sevens), Table 3 and Figure 3, which do not depend on the MoCA total score.
  • The verbal conclusions: top-ranked Level I algorithms are MoCA-based and mostly use Clock drawing and Animal naming; sMoCA achieves the highest balanced accuracy for Level II (FAQ total) classification.

Changed PDD rates

The corrected threshold changes the classification of 12 of 68 algorithms, all MoCA-based with IADL deficit defined by FAQ total score.

Corrected Tables A4 and A5

  • Table A4 (accuracy), corrected
  • Table A4, published
  • Table A5 (balanced accuracy), corrected
  • Table A5, published

Corrected manuscript

A corrected author version of the manuscript, generated from _manuscript/manuscript.qmd in this repository, is attached to the v2.0.0 release.
